title: Late-Credit Interest on Orthodontic Rider Credits — Premium Billing Accounts
content:
**Rule.** Interest is added to the credit on an ended Orthodontic Benefit Riders rider funded by a Premium Billing Accounts arrangement when the rider is credited late. The interest is added after any deduction and after the floor at 0.00; the credit is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Tiers by lateness** — the days from the rider's termination date to the credit date, in actual calendar days:
- more than 90 days: 15 percent a year of the rider interest base;
- more than 30 days but not more than 90: 10 percent a year of the rider interest base;
- 30 days or fewer: no interest.

**The rider interest base** is the rider premium (the ended rider's plan's monthly premium per covered person) reduced by the arrangement's prepay discount percentage (4 percent on Cascade Individual Annual Prepay, 0 percent on every other arrangement), for each prepaid month after the rider's termination date that is not among the rider months already credited — counted as the whole calendar months from that termination date to the paid-through date less the rider months already credited, never fewer than zero, and zero where no paid-through date is on record — running for the days from that termination date to the credit date beyond 30, on an actual-days basis over 365. In words: the discounted rider premium multiplied by those months, multiplied by the days beyond 30, divided by 365.

The rider months already credited are the months covered by termination credits on the rider line booked since the rider's termination month; a credit counts as booked since that month when the whole calendar months from its booking date to the credit date are no more than the whole calendar months from the rider's termination date to the credit date. Whole calendar months are counted the way an anniversary is counted (a month is complete only when a later month reaches the same day number, and the last day of a shorter month does not complete it).

**Boundary points.** 30 days: none. 31: 10 percent. 90: 10 percent. 91: 15 percent.

**Worked example (hypothetical).** Rider premium 27.35 on Cascade Individual Annual Prepay, so 26.256 after 4 percent; rider ended 30 April; paid through 31 December, 8 whole months; none already credited; credit date 8 August, 100 days after the end. Base: 26.256 multiplied by 8, multiplied by 70, divided by 365, about 40.2832. 100 days exceeds 90, so the interest is 15 percent, about 6.0425.
